long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Moscow in 1973, Sergey Brin moved with his family to the United States as a child. He studied mathematics and computer science at the University of Maryland, then pursued graduate computer science at Stanford. There he met Larry Page, and their work on ranking web pages by links developed into Google, which they incorporated in 1998. The search company's expansion and 2004 flotation made Brin one of the technology sector's wealthiest founders.

Brin later served as president of Alphabet, the holding company created above Google in 2015. He left that executive post in December 2019 but remains an Alphabet cofounder, board member and major voting shareholder; a 2026 filing showed that he and Page together controlled a majority of the company's voting power. His later philanthropy has concentrated heavily on scientific research, particularly Parkinson's disease and other neurological conditions.
